author: current Codex assistant
reasoning: A candidate has a chance iff allocating all remaining votes to that candidate places it among the top k positive-vote candidates, using the actual last-vote tie breaker. To test certainty, leave its current positive count unchanged and compute the minimum additional votes each rival needs to outrank it. Rivals already ahead cost0; every other rival receiving new votes must exceed its count because a new tied last vote is later. If the k cheapest rival costs fit the remaining budget, exclusion is possible. Zero-vote candidates are never treated as guaranteed merely because empty seats exist.
